[[F2-196]]'s question needs the follow-up *"and which of them is the server?"* |
| **⚠⚠ The browser had no transition table at all** | `transitionVuln` was `{ ...v, status }`. So `NEW → CLOSED` was permitted: a critical exposure marked closed having never been triaged, assigned, remediated or verified, with no `verified_by` and no audit row — the ECC remediation control itself, absent. Probed live: the server answers **409**. |
| **⚠ 31 of the 36 are past their ECC deadline and not closed, in dev and prod** | Including **all 9 open CRITICALs**. `GET ?overdueOnly=true` serves exactly that list and had no caller, so an almost entirely breached remediation register was invisible. The fabrication showed **one** overdue row — 🔑 **third consecutive instance of a fabrication erring in the flattering direction**, after [[F2-193]]'s cadences and [[F2-195]]'s KPI tiles. |
| **⚠⚠ A SECOND fabricated NCA regulator submission, and the reason F2-199's gate passed it** | `/cyber-lifecycle` emitted the *"NCA HASEEN — ECC v3 ANNUAL SELF-ASSESSMENT FILING"* **four ways**: a `.txt` download, a print-to-PDF stamped **"CONFIDENTIAL — REGULATOR"** with a reference id, and branded `.xlsx`/`.docx` through the platform's own export subsystem. Every figure came from `lib/cyberLifecycle.ts`'s browser constants. [[F2-199]]'s `exportProvenance` gate was **green over it** — and the reason is the reusable finding: the page's **only two** `SERVER_CALL` tokens were `reportingApi.packetXlsx(` and `reportingApi.packetDocx(`, and **both take the fabricated payload as their argument.** 🔑 **The server call the provenance gate found was the one carrying the invented figures out.** A rule that asks *does this page talk to a server?* cannot tell an inbound READ from an outbound WRITE, and at an export endpoint that difference is the entire question. |
| **⚠ Retired, not rewired — and the vulnerability half had to go with it** | `nca_ecc.filings` holds 4 real filings and `NcaEccFilingsPage` renders them at `/nca-ecc/filings` (ADR-017 §D-5, the answer [[F2-42]], [[F2-198]] and [[F2-199]] each reached). The ECC-filing half of the packet **cannot** be rebuilt: [[F2-199]] measured `responses_json` NULL on all 4 filings in both databases, so the per-control detail does not exist and inventing it is [[F2-196]]'s defect. 🔑 **Making only the vulnerability section real would have produced [[F2-203]]'s self-contradicting document — worse than a uniformly fabricated one, because the accurate half vouches for the other.** Both generators deleted; the header action now links to the real filing register. |
| **⚠⚠ SIX copies of the SLA matrix, and the sixth was found in the browser after the gate was green** | Five were in code and got deleted. The sixth is `cycVulnsSub` in **both** `en.ts` and `ar.ts`: *"Critical 7d / High 14d / Medium 30d / Low 60d… and asset tier (Tier-1 halves the window)"*. `SLA_DAYS` is **7 / 30 / 60 / 90**, so it told an operator HIGH was due in 14 days where the server had stamped 30 — **and there is no asset-tier rule in the server at all.** 🔑 **A claim about server behaviour can live anywhere a user reads text, and a gate scoped to code cannot see the one place written specifically to be read.** The gate now scans the translation files too, scoped to this module's keys (a scan not scoped to the shape of its claim invents findings — the recurring lesson here). Negative control run: the leg fires on the pre-fix string. |
| **⚠ F2-172(d)'s FIFTH instance, checked before writing a line** | `VulnerabilityService.create` was `req.getId() != null ? req.getId() : generateExternalId()` — a client could name the reference an NCA ECC reviewer cites, in a generator [[F2-48]] had **already** had to fix for collisions. Found by grepping `req.getId() != null ?` first, exactly as [[F2-204]]'s record instructs. 🔑 **An assumption that a family of defects is closed is the cheapest thing to check and the easiest to skip** — and it has now paid off twice running. |
| **⚠⚠ A REGRESSION MY OWN TWO PREVIOUS SLICES INTRODUCED AND NEITHER NOTICED** | `LifecycleOverviewPage` never hydrated anything. [[F2-203]] made `loadFindings()` return a cached server array and [[F2-204]] did the same for `loadTreatmentPlans()`; both replaced functions that had returned a seeded corpus **synchronously**. Every consumer that hydrates got real rows — and this page, which does not, silently began rendering an **empty internal-audit lane and an empty ERM treatment lane**. 🔑 [[F2-203]]'s own lesson turned on the slices that recorded it: **when you fix a store, a filter or a selector, assume something downstream has never run since, and run it.** It stayed invisible because an empty lane reads as a tenant with no rows rather than as a page that forgot to ask — [[F2-197]]'s *absence-reads-as-health*, one level up. Nothing in the type system can see a missing call, so it is now asserted. Confirmed in the browser: the page renders TP-2026-001…011 and F-2026-003 / FIN-001 again. |
| **⚠ A dark chain whose stated intent the machine forbids** | `chainSocEscalationToVuln` had **no caller anywhere**, and its own comment says it moves a row to `IN_REMEDIATION` *"instead of NEW/TRIAGED"* — a jump the machine reaches only from `OWNER_ASSIGNED`, so against the real register it is a 409 for exactly the rows it was written for. Browser-local the jump silently succeeded. Walking it legally needs **three attributed transitions**, which a side effect must not perform on a person's behalf, so the honest form is server-side ([[F2-190]]'s `hopVia`). Deleted with the reasoning recorded beside [[F2-202]]'s deletion of `chainBreachToDsr` in the same file. |
| **⚠⚠ THE MUTATION HARNESS FOUND TWO HOLES IN MY OWN NEW GATE, BOTH OF KINDS THIS REGISTER ALREADY NAMES** | **(1)** The terminal-set ban was `doesNotContain("List.of(\"CLOSED\")")` over the whole file — it banned **the exact literal I had just deleted**. A mutation writing `TERMINAL = Set.of("CLOSED")` and leaving the stream expression on an unused field SURVIVED. 🔑 [[F2-192]]'s headline in a gate written after quoting it: **a gate verifies the claim shape it was written for**, and banning the spelling you removed is not banning the defect. Re-scoped to `TERMINAL`'s **own initialiser**. **(2)** The hydration leg was `contains("hydrateVulns")`, and deleting all three call sites SURVIVED **because the name is still in the import list** — [[F2-194]]'s substring-satisfied-by-an-import, verbatim, in a gate written to catch a missing call. Now asserts the call shape. After both fixes: **16/16 mutations caught.** |
| **⚠ And a real miss in my own fix, caught by the gate one line from where I had fixed it** | I converted `bulkTriage` to ask `nextVulnStatuses` and left the BulkActionsBar's **enablement predicate** as `r.status === 'NEW'` — so the button's enabled state and the action's behaviour were two separate opinions about the same question, which is the defect this slice is about. 🔑 **A surface consults a status in more than one place, and the one deciding whether a control is OFFERED is the easy one to miss because it is not the one that does the work.** |
| **⚠ A gate leg failed on a correct tree because this codebase documents its deletions by quoting them** | `lifecycleStoreContract`'s derived-key leg read raw source, and the note explaining that `VULN_KEY = 'grc.cyber.vuln.v1'` is deleted **contains the key**, so the scan reported it as still written. 🔑 **A token-matching instrument over a codebase that explains its deletions will read the epitaph as the corpse** — same family as [[F2-193]] (a claim detector reading the sentence a correction quoted), [[F2-196]] (a page scan firing on its own correction comment) and [[F2-202]] (prose about code inventing callers). Both provenance gates and the new parity gate strip comments. Note the error **direction**: comment-blind over-reports, so it fails loudly rather than shrinking a population — the opposite of [[F2-198]]'s stripper bug. |
| **Gates** | New **`VulnerabilityMachineParityTest`** (backend, hermetic, **15 legs**): the FE table compared to `VulnerabilityService.ALLOWED` **edge-for-edge by reflection in both directions**; the `VulnStatus` union and the `TransitionRequest` `@Pattern` each asserted equal to the machine's state set; the terminal set asserted **derived on both sides**; every `VULN_PRIMARY_PATH` step required to be a legal edge and to cover every non-terminal state; every state required to carry a bilingual label and a tone; no surface may hold a second table or a per-status control branch; the SLA matrix banned in pages **and translations**; the minted reference; the retired Haseen generators; the realtime handler; a positive control feeding every pre-fix shape back in; and a both-directions test of the comment stripper. New **`vulnerabilityLifecycle.test.ts`** (frontend, **16 legs**) covering the predicates' behaviour, including that an unrecognised status reads as OPEN and that `isVulnStatusManaged('constructor')` is false. |
| **Ratchets** | clientless endpoints **410 → 408**, guarded writes **200 → 199** · `BASELINE_ENDPOINT_BEARING_NOT_WIRED` **6 → 5** · `cyber-vulnerabilities` **BROWSER_LOCAL → SERVER_BACKED** (registry SERVER_BACKED list asserted exactly, now 3) · `exportProvenance` **hard zero retired** — see below. |
| **⚠⚠ The export gate's hard zero could not be kept, and saying why is the honest move** | Correcting the direction-blindness moved that population from 9 backed / **0** unbacked to 9 backed / **2** unbacked: `/crisis-management` emits an **NCEMA** crisis packet and `/bcm-lifecycle` a **SAMA operational-resilience** packet, each three ways, each from browser constants, each previously certified for the same reason. Neither is new code. The gate's own comment said *"if a member is ever added, delete this assertion in the same commit and say why"* — this is that commit. Both are recorded as measured, **filed defects** in an exactly-asserted, decrease-only map, not as designs. The BCM one is **not wireable by a frontend slice**: three of its four registers are the `NO_SERVER_SURFACE` stores [[F2-204]] measured (21 rows, no controller). 🔑 [[F2-204]]'s rule, pointing the other way: there the ratchet's *question* was wrong; here the question was right and the **answer** was under-measured, so the number moves and says so. **A hard zero over a population the instrument cannot see is the most reassuring possible artefact.** |
| **Verified** | FE **688/688 across 62 files** (671→688), `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean. Backend **3,821 / 0 failures**. **Mutation 16/16 caught** after the two self-inflicted holes were closed. **Live probe 32/32** with `so_officer` (CYBER read+write) and `ranalyst` (403 on both read and write) — never `admin`: the client-chosen reference refused and a `VULN-2026-…` minted instead, `NEW → CLOSED` **409**, `ACCEPTED` **400** at the boundary, the full legal walk NEW→TRIAGED→OWNER_ASSIGNED→IN_REMEDIATION→AWAITING_VERIFICATION→CLOSED with `triagedBy`/`verifiedBy` = `so_officer` and a HIGH deadline stamped at +30 days, `FALSE_POSITIVE` from NEW with its bilingual reason stored, `RISK_ACCEPTED` from TRIAGED with the acceptor taken from the principal **and the body's invented `'Sara Al-Zahrani (CISO)'` ignored**, `RISK_ACCEPTED → IN_REMEDIATION` **409**, a fresh GET still CLOSED, the DB row agreeing, `?overdueOnly=true` returning exactly 31, and the register served through the Vite proxy. |
| **Browser-verified** | All 39 rows render from the server; every row's controls are exactly its machine edges (NEW → *Triaged / False positive*; TRIAGED → *Owner assigned / Risk accepted / False positive*; AWAITING_VERIFICATION → *Closed / In remediation*); statuses render **bilingually** (`مقبولة كمخاطرة`, `إنذار كاذب`); the workspace KPI strip shows the real **9** open criticals and **31** overdue; and `LifecycleOverviewPage` renders real treatment plans and findings again. **A transition clicked in the browser POSTed to `/api/cyber-lc/vulnerabilities/{id}/transition` and the server answered 403** for a persona without `CYBER:WRITE` — and **neither the screen nor the database changed**, which is the exact inverse of the defect: the old code would have shown success and mutated the row for that same persona. |
| **⚠ Two things the browser found that the gates could not** | The status column had **no cell renderer**, so an Arabic-primary UI printed `RISK_ACCEPTED` (house rule 7); and the "by status" chart used raw tokens as axis labels **and** ordered categories by whatever the server returned first — [[F2-197]]'s *declaration order dressed up as meaning*. Both now read through the total-function label and the derived state order. |
| **⚠ Left behind, deliberately** | Three `[REVIEW-TEST]` vulnerabilities in dev tenant 1 (`VULN-2026-19FFAD8FBF22CC2` CLOSED, `…D06235D` FALSE_POSITIVE, `…D4426E1` RISK_ACCEPTED). Deleting them is a destructive DB operation and needs the owner's explicit OK (house rule 6). **No seeded row was altered** — the browser transition was aimed at a probe row and was refused anyway. |
| **Filed** | **(a)** **The two-registers-one-object question, unresolved and now sharper.** `cyber.vulnerabilities` (**21 rows**, `/api/v1/cyber/vulnerabilities`, rendered by `CyberPage`) and `cyber_lc.vulnerabilities` (**36 rows**, this slice) are both live, both real, and not the same object at the same fidelity — only the second has the ECC machine, the SLA deadline and the three attribution columns. Plus `cyber.vulnerability_sla_finding` (11), `cyber.vulnerability_sla_policy` (4) and `cyber.vuln_exceptions` (3). **Which register the platform reports to the NCA is an owner decision** ([[F2-196]]). **(b)** the two unbacked regulator/authority emitters above. **(c)** `cyber_lc` has **zero CHECK constraints** in the whole schema; all 36 stored statuses are in the machine today, so it is latent — but [[F2-183]]'s rule applies (a CHECK and its writer land together). **(d)** the five remaining browser-local corpora in `cyberLifecycle.ts` — ECC filing, assets, threats, SOC alerts, pen tests — and the filing tab still transitions a local store; **its two invented officers were removed in this slice** so whoever wires `nca_ecc.filings` does not inherit [[F2-204]]'s trap. **(e)** `risk_accepted_by` is NULL on all four `RISK_ACCEPTED` rows, so the register carries four unattributed acceptances; the page discloses that rather than inventing one. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED for the ECC vulnerability register.** Store **BROWSER_LOCAL → SERVER_BACKED**; three consumer pages and one chain repointed; five client vocabularies collapsed to one mirrored, gated table; two `FALSE_POSITIVE`/`RISK_ACCEPTED` dispositions made reachable for the first time; a second fabricated NCA submission retired; F2-172(d)'s fifth instance closed; a two-slice-old regression on the overview page closed. 1 backend file + 1 new backend gate, 7 frontend files + 1 new frontend gate, 2 translation files, 0 migrations. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A live wire that terminates in a constant reads, from either end, as an integration that works.** The subscription was real, the topic matched the broadcaster's format string exactly, the frame arrived — and the handler re-read `localStorage`. Nothing that measures *whether a symbol is called*, *whether a page calls a server*, or *whether a document has server data in scope* can see that, because every component of it is genuine except the direction the data flows. Corollary, from the export gate: **the server call a provenance rule finds may be the one carrying the fabrication out** — so ask not *does this talk to a server?* but *does this READ from one?* And the third, from five client vocabularies that all agreed with each other: **consistency among copies is not evidence, it is the mechanism of concealment.** |

## F2-204 · The lifecycle-store registry declared 6 of 16 browser-local corpora, seven populated registers have no endpoint at all, and the ERM treatment-plan approval wrote nothing

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-204 *(measured 2026-08-13, the population [[F2-202]] filed and [[F2-203]] began. Lineage: [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-199]] → [[F2-201]] → [[F2-202]] → [[F2-203]] → this.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2 for the registry, P1 for the approval.** The instrument half is a defect in an artefact I shipped one slice earlier; the wire half is [[F2-201]]/[[F2-203]]'s shape on a third governance control, and the page invented the *substance* of the decision, not only its author. |
| **🔑 The registry declared 6 corpora when the four modules own 16** | `lib/lifecycleStores.ts` listed exactly the corpora that happen to have a controller — a coherent rule I never stated and therefore never checked — so ten were invisible, and `BASELINE_BROWSER_LOCAL_STORES = 6` read as *"6 stores remain"* against a real 16. Measured from the modules' own localStorage keys: `privacyLifecycle` 3, `riskLifecycle` 3, `bcmLifecycle` 4, `cyberLifecycle` 6. **A registry that declares one member per module reads exactly like a registry that declares them all** — [[F2-198]]'s finding about `demoFallbackContract` (*"the invariant is real, its POPULATION is a filename pattern"*), committed in the artefact built to replace that decoy. The coverage leg now **derives** the population from those keys, so a corpus cannot be omitted by not being thought of. |
| **⚠⚠ Seven registers are populated and have no endpoint of any kind — 69 rows in dev AND prod** | `risk_lc.kri_breaches` **12** · `bcm_lc.bia_records` **8** · `bcm_lc.recovery_strategies` **8** · `bcm_lc.drills` **5** · `cyber_lc.assets` **14** · `cyber_lc.cyber_incidents` **10** · `cyber_lc.threat_intel` **12**. No controller, no service, and for six of them no entity. Resolved by searching **every** `@RequestMapping` path, not by looking under `module/*_lc/` — because similar objects DO have controllers in other modules over DIFFERENT tables (`/api/v1/bcm/bia-assessments`, `/api/v1/socops/ot-assets`, `/api/v1/cyber/threat-intel`), which is [[F2-196]]'s disjoint-register shape and exactly what makes *"there is no endpoint"* easy to get wrong in the reassuring direction. New `NO_SERVER_SURFACE` state: **an unwireable store and an unwired one are different facts**, and collapsing them makes the next slice re-measure everything. |
| **⚠⚠ A decrease-only ratchet cannot express "the population was undercounted"** | Declaring the real 16 would have meant raising `BASELINE_NOT_FULLY_SERVER_BACKED` from 6 to 17 — **indistinguishable from tolerating a regression.** So no figure was raised: the ratchet was **re-scoped** to *stores that have an endpoint and still do not write to it* (7 → **6**, honestly decreasing), the unwireable population got its own decrease-only figure (**9**), and the total is asserted **exactly** so the next omission fails rather than shrinks a count. 🔑 When a ratchet's number must go up, the question is whether its *question* was wrong. |
| **The wire: an ERM approval that wrote nothing** | `risk_lc.treatment_plans` holds **10 live rows** (9 in tenant 1) behind a complete, hardened controller — GET, GET `/{id}`, POST, POST `/{id}/transition`, DELETE, each `hasPermission('RISK', …)` under `@RequireModule("RISK")`, with a `Map<String, Set<String>> ALLOWED` machine answering 409. `transitionPlan` is the sign-off on **how a risk will be treated** (`DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED`) and every decision went to localStorage. Third instance of [[F2-201]]'s inverse shape in three slices. |
| **⚠⚠ The page invented the SUBSTANCE of the decision, not just its author** | It passed `'Mohammed Al-Mahmoud (CRO)'` as the approving Chief Risk Officer **and** the literal `'Insufficient cost-benefit justification'` as the rejection reason. The server **persists** `rejectedReason`, so **wiring this naively would have written invented text into `risk_lc.treatment_plans.rejected_reason` as a real officer's stated rationale.** Both removed: the approver is the authenticated principal (F2-22b(vi) already did this server-side), and a rejection reason now comes from the rejecting officer or not at all — there is no input for one on that card, so it is filed rather than defaulted. Fourth invented officer in three slices, after the AC chair, audit manager and auditor of [[F2-203]]. |
| **⚠⚠ An undo affordance over a server-enforced machine is a promise the machine forbids** | The page's undoable toast called `transitionPlan(planId, priorStatus)` — a **backwards** transition. The machine allows exactly one reverse edge (`REJECTED → DRAFT`), so un-submitting, un-approving and un-completing would each answer **409** (probed: `APPROVED → SUBMITTED` is 409). While the store was browser-local the undo silently worked and the register drifted from anything the machine would ever have permitted. Removed; if reversal is a requirement it is a reverse **edge** plus an audit reason, decided on the server. |
| **⚠ Two more copies of the machine** | An `onAdvance` lookup map and an `onBulkAdvance` lookup map — the fourth and fifth in this programme's frontends after [[F2-203]]'s four. Both derive from one table now, and the bulk path is sequential so a partial failure is reported rather than swallowed. **11 hard-coded status-equality button conditions** deleted across the two slices. |
| **⚠⚠ MY OWN GATE REFUTED TWO OF MY ELEVEN CLAIMS ON ITS FIRST RUN** | `noServerSurfaceStoresReallyHaveNone` verifies the claim *structurally* — a controller cannot serve a table no `@Entity` maps to — and it fired on **`socops.pentest_engagement`** (served at `/api/v1/socops/pentests`; the store is ordinary `BROWSER_LOCAL`) and **`risk_lc.treatment_actions`** (a `TreatmentAction` entity exists). | **⚠⚠ And the second refutation exposed a claim I had already written into three places** | Chasing `treatment_actions` showed the **server's** `TreatmentPlanDto` declares `List<TreatmentActionDto> actions` and maps all 10 rows on every read. The registry's `rowsDev` is a *register size*; what a persona sees is a different number, and a probe that asserts the first against the second fails on correct code. |

Deriving the risk from a finding's control crosswalk is a product decision ([[F2-201]]'s precedent for `chainBreachToDsr`). The CAPA half is a real write and stays. |
| **Gates** | `lifecycleStoreContract.test.ts` **31 legs** — the coverage leg derives the population from the modules' keys; the unwireable leg requires `endpoint === ''` and refuses any endpoint-bearing store claiming to be unserved; the reverse key leg was **re-scoped from per-module to per-corpus** (it asserted a `localKey: ''` store's module writes no keys at all, which held only while every module hosted one store — the same per-unit defect [[F2-203]] fixed in its disclosure leg, failing loudly here rather than silently). Backend `LifecycleStoreBackingContractTest` **7 legs**, with the new structural verification of every `NO_SERVER_SURFACE` claim. |
| **Ratchets** | `BASELINE_ENDPOINT_BEARING_NOT_WIRED` **7 → 6** (re-scoped, see above) · `BASELINE_NO_SERVER_SURFACE` **9** (new, decrease-only; 11 claimed, 2 refuted) · `DECLARED_CORPORA` **18** exact · `BASELINE_BROWSER_LOCAL_STORES` **6** · clientless endpoints **411 → 410**, guarded writes **201 → 200** · census `fe_pages` **352 → 353**. |
| **⚠ F2-16 refused a page for the second consecutive slice** | The rewire took `RiskLifecyclePage.tsx` to **807** lines and `sourceFileSizeRatchet` said *"Split it rather than adding it"* — as it did to `AuditLifecyclePage` in [[F2-203]]. | **Verified** | FE **671/671 across 61 files**, `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean. The last is not a plain wire: `socops` owns that register, so it is [[F2-196]]'s two-registers-one-object question. **(b)** the **9 unwireable stores** — 69 rows in seven populated registers with no endpoint; building one is backend work, and `noServerSurfaceStoresReallyHaveNone` will fire the moment an entity appears, which is the signal that slice needs. **(c)** the treatment-**actions** sub-resource: reads work, no write surface exists. **(d)** `risk_lc.acceptance_requests` is **empty in both databases** while `transitionAcceptance` runs a CRO-and-board sign-off in the browser — a governance decision with no register at all. **(e)** `risk_lc.kri_escalation_log` is empty, so no KRI escalation has ever been recorded server-side. **(f)** the finding→risk chain's missing derivation. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED for the treatment-plan register, the registry's population, and the four invented-identity/invented-substance sites.** 1 store to `PARTIALLY_SERVER_BACKED` (reads and decisions wired; the action sub-resource does not exist). Registry **6 → 18 declared corpora** with a state vocabulary that distinguishes unwired from unwireable. 3 backend files, 6 frontend files, 1 new page module, 2 gates re-scoped. **OPEN as a population: 6 wireable, 9 unwireable.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A registry is only as honest as the rule that decided its membership, and that rule is usually implicit.** Mine admitted a corpus if it had a controller — never stated, never checked, and it hid ten of sixteen while looking complete. The fix is not a bigger list but a **derived** population: the gate now reads the modules' own localStorage keys, so membership is a measurement rather than a recollection. Corollary, from the two claims my own gate refuted and the one the probe refuted: **the parts of a new instrument most likely to be wrong are the claims it was built to check** — so verify them structurally in the same commit, and expect roughly two in ten to fall. |

## F2-203 · The internal-audit workspace: closing a finding wrote nothing, every list was empty on every engagement, and all four registers hold statuses no artefact declares

|  |  |
|---|---|

Mutation 32/32; pre-fix control 21/21; live probe 33/33; browser flow verified across all six tabs. **OPEN as an owner decision: the vocabularies and the code spaces.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A latent crash in a display path is held shut by whatever else is broken around it — so fixing one defect can be what detonates the next.** Three label-map TypeErrors sat in this module, each on a real row, none reachable: one behind a filter that removed every row, one behind an insertion-order accident, one behind a ternary. The slice's own plan-selection fix opened the second, in the browser, minutes after the gate went green. **When you fix a filter, a selector or a fallback, assume something downstream has never run — and run it.** Corollary on instruments: after *does this page call a server?* ([[F2-198]]), *does this file emit a document?* ([[F2-199]]) and *does the call reach anything?* ([[F2-202]]), ask **which of this file's data reaches the thing it emits** — a one-hop provenance rule certifies the file, not the figure.

## F2-202 · A persistence-mode switch with no setter: five lifecycle workspaces called a REST mirror that could never send, and the Knowledge Base list was empty while 21 articles were published

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-202 *(measured 2026-08-13, the item [[F2-201]] filed as needing its own slice. Lineage: [[F2-42]] → [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-199]] → [[F2-201]] → this. F2-200 is the browser-local MFA item [[F2-199]] filed and is still open.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2 for the mechanism, and it contained one live P2 defect on a working module.** Every finding before this one in the lineage was a fabrication *displayed*; [[F2-201]] was an action *accepted*. This one is a **mechanism that made five workspaces look persistent while being unable to persist**, plus one concrete consequence a user hits today: the Knowledge Base list was permanently empty. |
| **The switch, measured** | `lib/platformPersistence.ts` declared `PersistenceMode = 'demo' \| 'rest' \| 'mixed'`, persisted under `grc.persistence.mode.v1`, and exported three `mirror*ToBackend` helpers that `return` immediately when the mode is `'demo'`. **`setPersistenceMode` had ZERO callers anywhere in the product; nothing wrote the localStorage key; the switch took no Vite env input.** So `'demo'` was not a *default* — it was an **invariant**, in every build, for every user, and all three mirror helpers were unconditional no-ops called from 11 sites across 5 modules. |
| **⚠⚠ And the READ path never consulted the mode at all** | `loadTreatmentPlans()` and its four siblings read localStorage unconditionally. So even with a reachable switch, a write that reached the server could never be **shown**. 🔑 **Writing to a store you never read from is not persistence, it is a one-way drain** — the mechanism was incoherent in principle as well as inert in practice. Only one export was mode-aware on a read (`adapterListAll`, 1 consumer), and that one caused the live defect below. |
| **⚠⚠ There are TWO mode switches and the badge reads the other one** | The topbar `ModeBadge` reads `lib/productionMode.ts` — `'demo' \| 'migrating' \| 'production'`, key `grc.mode.v1`, and it **does** take `VITE_MODE`. `platformPersistence.ts`'s own header claimed *"Drives the ModeBadge in the topbar."* It did not, and never had. **A deployment could set `VITE_MODE=production`, turn the badge green and label it "Production", while the switch that gated every lifecycle write stayed `'demo'` and unreachable.** [[F2-184]]'s shape — a comment answering the question a reader was about to ask — on the file's first line. |
| **⚠ A THIRD file with the same type name** | `lib/persistence.ts` declares its own `PersistenceMode` (a third distinct union) over `/api/v1/persistence/{key}`. That controller is real; `platform.persistence_row` holds **exactly 1 row, `store_key = 'demo-key'`** in dev — the endpoint has only ever received a test row. Its `PERSISTENCE_REGISTRY` carries hand-set `backendReady` booleans, which is [[F2-193]]'s status-word-nobody-feeds shape; filed, not fixed. |
| **🔑 The live defect: the Knowledge Base list was empty while 21 articles were published** | `kb.ts` sends **every** call to the real server — `getArticle`, `createArticle`, `updateArticle`, `transitionArticle`, `deleteArticle` — except `listArticles()`, which went through `adapterListAll(KB_ARTICLE_ADAPTER, [])` → stuck `'demo'` mode → `loadLocal('grc.kb.articles.v1', [])` → an empty localStorage key → **`[]`**. Probed live: `kb.articles` holds **22 rows, 21 PUBLISHED**, and `GET /api/kb/articles` returns all 21. So an author could create an article, watch it persist, open it by slug, publish it — and never see it in the list. **`KbHomePage` carried a comment reading *"falls back to localStorage seed (empty until articles are published)"*, which explained the symptom away with a cause that was not the cause.** Fixed by one line: `api.get<KbArticle[]>('/api/kb/articles')`. |
| **The twelve real registers behind the twelve adapters** | All twelve `restEndpoint` paths resolve to live controllers, and all are populated (dev, identical in prod unless noted): `risk_lc.treatment_plans` **11** · `audit_lc.findings` **20** · `privacy_lc.dsr_cases` **12** · `bcm_lc.invocations` **3** · `cyber_lc.vulnerabilities` **36** · `approvals.requests` **22** ([[F2-201]] wired it) · `capa.tasks` **14** · `regchange.changes` **14** · `kb.articles` **22** · `audit_eng.engagements` **1** · `board_pack.packs` **16** · `nca_ecc.filings` **4**. Six adapters had no consumer at all beyond the `LIFECYCLE_ADAPTERS` map, which itself had **zero** consumers despite its comment claiming the ModeBadge iterates it. |
| **⚠⚠ The adapters were wrong about their own localStorage keys — 3 of 5** | `BCM_INVOCATION_ADAPTER` named `grc.bcm.invocations.v1` where the module writes `grc.bcm.invocation.v1` (singular); `CYBER_VULN_ADAPTER` named `grc.cyber.vulnerabilities.v1` where the module writes `grc.cyber.vuln.v1`; `AUDIT_FINDING_ADAPTER` named `grc.audit.findings.v1` for a module that **keeps no localStorage key at all**. Had the switch ever been reachable, `adapterListAll` would have read three keys nothing had ever written and returned its seed. 🔑 **Independent confirmation that the mechanism was never once exercised** — and it was found only because the new gate checks each declared key against its module's source. |
| **Fix — the rewire** | The **DSR (PDPL Article 4) workspace**, chosen because it is [[F2-196]]'s own named residue, it is statutory, and it is [[F2-201]]'s inverse shape again: a hardened server side with no client. New `lib/privacyLcApi.ts` + the DSR half of `PrivacyLifecyclePage` and the lifecycle overview now read `/api/privacy-lc/dsr-cases`, decide through `POST /{id}/transition`, and replace the row **from the server's response**. `SEED_DSR`'s three clock-minted cases, `loadDsr`/`saveDsr`/`createDsr`/`transitionDsr`/`dsrSlaRemaining` and the DSR label maps are deleted from `privacyLifecycle.ts`. |
| **⚠⚠ THREE client-side minters of a statutory deadline, all deleted** | `createDsr()` minted the PDPL Article 4 30-day deadline as `Date.now() + 30 * 86_400_000` **and** the tracking reference as `DSR-<year>-<Math.random()*999>` — three digits of entropy, so two subjects filing the same day could collide on one reference. The page's Extend handler recomputed the 60-day extension **and invented the extension justification on the operator's behalf**. And `lifecycleChains.ts#chainBreachToDsr` was a third, with no callers. [[F2-172]] settled this rule for the intake substrate — *only the server may issue a tracking code or a statutory deadline* — and **deleted the client minters rather than moving them**. Same here. |
| **⚠ Two server-side defects fixed with it** | `DsrCaseService.create` was `d.setExternalId(req.getId() != null ? req.getId() : generateExternalId())` — **it honoured a client-supplied reference code for a statutory request**, [[F2-172]](d)'s exact defect. The caller's `id` is now ignored outright; nothing supplied one (no client existed, no test sets one), so refusing it cannot break a working caller. And `TransitionRequest` had **no field for a rejection reason**, so a lawful PDPL Article 4 refusal could never be recorded — the columns had existed since V17 with nothing able to write them. |
| **⚠ Two columns were on the table and not on the wire** | `sla_breached_at` and `rejection_reason_en/ar` exist since V17 and `DsrCaseDto` never declared them — [[F2-198]]'s `crossBorderTransfer` shape, where a field is already in the table and the wire merely never mentions it. **`slaBreachedAt` is not the same question as "is the deadline past"**, and the difference is measurable right now: dev's two `EXTENDED` cases carry a breach stamp, **prod's two do not**, because [[F2-196]]'s sweep fix has not been deployed. A client deriving breach from its own clock cannot show that gap; the page now has a separate `pastDeadlineUnrecorded` tile that does. |
| **Fix — the fingerprint, because deleting a decoy removes one** | Deleting 11 no-op mirror calls is right; deleting them and stopping would leave five workspaces looking like ordinary local state with a real populated register behind each. So the trace moved into `lib/lifecycleStores.ts`: **8 stores**, each declaring its state, the REST base of the real register, `schema.table`, measured dev/prod row counts, its localStorage key and a consequence-naming note. `lib/platformPersistence.ts` is **deleted**. |
| **⚠⚠ A THIRD state exists and the first draft of the registry missed it** | `auditLifecycle.ts` **reads the server** — `hydrateAuditLifecycle()` fetches four `/api/audit-lc/*` resources — and writes a module-level array. So its list is real and every mutation evaporates on reload, which is *harder* to notice than an honestly local store because the list looks right. It also carries `if (_findings.length === 0) _findings = SEED_FINDINGS`, the [[F2-158]] fallback shape: a tenant with an empty register sees invented findings. `SERVER_READ_LOCAL_WRITE` is tracked by its own decrease-only figure, because collapsing it into "browser-local" would let a reclassification read as progress. |
| **The gates — two halves, neither sufficient** | `lifecycleStoreContract.test.ts` (frontend, 28 legs) holds what only the frontend knows: the browser-local subset is **derived** not hand-listed, `DSR_TERMINAL` is **derived** from the transition table, `isOpen` is the **complement** of it, the create payload carries no `id` and no `slaDeadline`, no arithmetic anywhere produces a 30-day window, an unread register renders **unmeasured** rather than zero, action buttons come from `DSR_ALLOWED` rather than status-equality tests, `useApiList` is refused on the page, and — the load-bearing leg — **no decision may be written into local state**. `LifecycleStoreBackingContractTest` (backend, hermetic, 6 legs) resolves every declared `endpoint` to a real controller and refuses the resurrection of the deleted switch. |
| **⚠⚠ The backend leg is not decoration: I guessed 3 of 8 endpoint paths from the schema name and got all three wrong** | `/api/privacy/ropa` is really `/api/v1/privacy/ropa`; the DPIA controller is at `/api/v1/privacy/dpias` — **plural, its own class**, not a sub-path; cross-border is `/api/privacy/cross-border-transfers` with **no `v1` segment at all**. Each looked entirely plausible in a reviewed file. 🔑 **A schema name does not predict a path, and a plausible endpoint string in a declared registry is worth nothing until something resolves it.** Fourth guessed-path error in this lineage after [[F2-197]]'s tables, [[F2-198]]'s tables and [[F2-199]]'s columns — and the first one a gate caught instead of a probe. |
| **⚠⚠ My registry's PROSE created a phantom caller in a reachability scan** | `apiClientReachability` reported `lib/lifecycleStores.ts` as an API client with no importer (its `/api/...` strings are **data**), and separately reported `hydrateAuditLifecycle` as *now called* — because a note explaining what that function fetches put the token in a production file, and "called" there is a deliberate token match. 🔑 **Prose about code, stored as data, invents callers in a token-matching scan.** Fixed by a `DECLARATIVE_REGISTRIES` exclusion that is checked in both directions: a file may only be excluded if it contains **no real `api.*` call**, proven by its own mutation. |
| **⚠ Three of my own errors, each caught by running something** | (a) The `loadDsr\|saveDsr\|transitionDsr` ban **fired on the page's own `loadDsrCases()`** — a substring match satisfied by something other than its claim, in the gate written to catch that class of thing; word anchors fixed it. (b) The quotation trap: my correction **quotes** the sentence it replaces, so the detector read the quotation as the claim and failed the fix. [[F2-193]] solved this with `unquoted()`; my first `unquoted()` excluded newlines from the span, so a quotation wrapped across two lines of a block comment still fired. (c) A retained-explanation assertion matched prose that wraps; it now matches a sentinel (`F2-202-EMPTY-KEY`) that appears nowhere else. |
| **⚠ And a ratchet set one too loose** | `BASELINE_BROWSER_LOCAL_STORES` was written as 7 by counting entries *before* `audit-findings` was reclassified; the detector returns **6**. Corrected against the running app. [[F2-195]]'s lesson holds: a baseline lifted from a measurement of something else is worse than no baseline, because it looks measured. |
| **Ratchets** | `BASELINE_BROWSER_LOCAL_STORES` **6**, `BASELINE_NOT_FULLY_SERVER_BACKED` **7** of 8 (both new, decrease-only). `FrontendEndpointContractTest`: clientless endpoints **417 → 413**, clientless guarded writes **206 → 203** — the gate fired *downward* and named the new figures. `apiClientReachability`: the 8 `platformPersistence` entries are gone from `KNOWN_UNREACHED` (11 → 3 in its platform-services group). |
| **Verified** | FE **619/619 across 60 files** (+29), `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean. Backend **3796 tests** (+6). Mutation **19/19 as declared** — 17 caught, 1 declared SURVIVES control (reordering a transition list, since membership is what `mayTransition` tests), and one MISSED on the first pass that was **the mutation's fault**: it inserted `useApiList` as a *comment*, which the gate correctly strips, so it had not reintroduced anything ([[F2-197]]'s rule that a control which does not break the thing proves nothing). **Live probe 24/24**, and from the running browser: `platformPersistence.ts` fails to import; `dsrApi.get`/`listOverdue` are `undefined`; `DSR_TERMINAL` is `["DELIVERED","REJECTED"]` derived; `isOpen('EXTENDED')` true and an unrecognised status also true (the safe direction for a statutory clock); a case filed through the page got a **server-minted** reference `DSR-2026-19FF892FA317AED` and deadline `2026-09-12`; `INTAKE → DELIVERED` was refused **409**; the Article 4 extension moved the deadline `2026-09-12 → 2026-10-12`, **exactly 30 days added server-side**; a fresh read still showed it; and `listArticles()` returned **21** where it returned 0 before. |
| **⚠ Left behind, deliberately** | Four `[REVIEW-TEST]`-tagged rows in dev `privacy_lc.dsr_cases` (three `ACCESS` from the probe, one `PORTABILITY` from the browser flow). Deleting them is a destructive DB operation and needs the owner's explicit OK (house rule 6). |
| **Filed** | **(a)** the **7 remaining stores** in the new registry — 6 browser-local (`privacy-ropa`, `privacy-dpia`, `privacy-cbt`, `risk-treatment`, `bcm-invocations`, `cyber-vulnerabilities`) and 1 `SERVER_READ_LOCAL_WRITE` (`audit-findings`), each with its endpoint and row count already resolved. `risk-treatment` is the awkward one: `lib/api.ts` **already** calls `GET/POST /api/risk-lc/treatment-plans`, so the risk detail view and the lifecycle workspace read two different stores for the same plans — wiring it means reconciling two callers, not adding one. **(b)** `lib/persistence.ts` + `PERSISTENCE_REGISTRY`'s hand-set `backendReady` booleans over a table holding one `'demo-key'` row. **(c)** `lib/productionMode.ts` is read by **`ProductionReadinessPage`, a Sprint 4 §3.3 culled page**, plus `fileUpload.ts` and the badge; whether a mode badge should exist at all once the stores are wired is an owner call. **(d)** the breach-to-DSR chain the deleted `chainBreachToDsr` named — a real capability, but *which subjects get notified* is a product decision, not plumbing. **(e)** `POST /api/privacy-lc/dsr-cases` answers **200, not 201** (`ResponseEntity.ok`); cosmetic, and asserting the REST-correct status would have failed on working code. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED for the DSR workspace, the Knowledge Base list and the switch itself; OPEN as a population of 7 stores.** `lib/platformPersistence.ts` deleted, 11 no-op mirror sites removed, `lib/lifecycleStores.ts` + two gates shipped (frontend 28 legs, backend 6 legs, both directions enforced). Mutation 19/19 as declared; live probe 24/24; browser flow verified end to end. The 7 remaining stores are declared with their real endpoint and measured row count rather than left implicit. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A reachability scan measures whether a symbol is *called*, never whether calling it *does anything*.** `apiClientReachability` correctly reported all eight `platformPersistence` adapters as unreached for months and that was tolerated, because "an adapter nothing calls" reads as unfinished plumbing. The three `mirror*ToBackend` helpers had callers in five modules, so they never appeared in that scan at all — and every one of them returned before sending. **The second question is where the defect was, and no instrument here asked it.** Corollary for this lineage's tenth instrument: after asking *does this page call a server?* ([[F2-198]]) and *does this file emit a document?* ([[F2-199]]), ask **does the call it makes reach anything?** |

## F2-201 · A governance control reported success without acting: the approval inbox decided 12 invented requests in React state while 12 real ones sat unseen

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-201 *(measured 2026-08-12, immediately after [[F2-199]] — the second of the eleven pages [[F2-198]] filed. Lineage: [[F2-42]] → [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-199]] → this. F2-200 is the browser-local MFA item [[F2-199]] filed and is still open.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2, and the sharpest kind so far.** Every earlier finding in this lineage showed a false figure. This one accepted an **action**: an approver clicked Approve on a policy publication or a risk acceptance, got a success toast plus a second toast claiming downstream chain rules had fired, and **nothing was written anywhere**. A reload put the request back to PENDING. Not P1 only because no control is *bypassed* — the real register was untouched, so nothing was wrongly approved; the harm is that a duty was believed discharged and the real queue was invisible. |
| **What was wrong, measured** | `/approvals` (`ApprovalInboxPage` 326 lines + `lib/approvals.ts` 407) was **routed, sidebar-linked and made no server call of any kind**. `lib/approvals.ts` was an approval **engine** in the browser: **12 hard-coded requests** `AP-001`…`AP-012`, clock-minted from `const _now = Date.now()` at module load; a **16-role `APPROVER_REGISTRY`** naming invented individuals as the organisation's CISO, DPO, CFO, CEO, CHRO, COO, CIO and General Counsel; and a `PARALLEL_ANY` / `PARALLEL_ALL` / `SEQUENTIAL` routing machine with a per-approver `decisions[]` progress bar. Its own comment called it *"Demo data — 12 pending approvals across the platform"*. `decide()` and `delegate()` mutated `setRequests` and returned. |
| **The real register, probed live** | `approvals.requests` holds **22 rows in dev** — 12 PENDING / 9 APPROVED / 1 DELEGATED — and **21 in prod** (11 PENDING), assigned to real dev personas (`admin` 7, `auditor`, `compliance`, `riskmanager`) plus named external reviewers, across **17 real `entity_type` values** (POLICY, RISK_ACCEPTANCE, CAPA, BOARD_PACK, PDPL_DPIA, AUDIT_FINDING, VENDOR_ONBOARD, AI_MODEL…). `sla_deadline` is populated on **12 of 22**. None of it appeared on this page. |
| **🔑 The INVERSE of [[F2-198]] and [[F2-199]], and that is what made it worst** | Those two were fabrications where a real surface already existed, so the fix was to retire. Here there was **a complete server side with no client at all**: `ApprovalRequestController` exposes list / `?myInbox=true` / create / transition / delete, and it was **hardened before the fabrication was written** — the controller's own comment records S2 (F-1) closing a wide-open transition, SEC-IAM-002 takes the deciding identity from the authenticated principal and *never* a body field, and `ApprovalRequestService` refuses a decision from anyone but the current assignee. The browser copy was not filling a gap; it was **shadowing a finished control**, using the same type name (`ApprovalRequest`) as the server entity. |
| **Fix — the first member of this population REWIRED rather than retired** | New `lib/approvalsApi.ts` (the client + the server's state machine); `ApprovalInboxPage` now loads the real register, offers a **"Only mine"** toggle backed by `?myInbox=true`, and decides through `POST /{id}/transition` with the row replaced **from the server's response**. `lib/approvals.ts` deleted. **0 backend changes, 0 migrations** — everything needed already shipped. |
| **⚠ Deliberately SIMPLER than what it replaced** | The server carries one `assigned_to` at a time plus `delegated_from`. There are no parallel/sequential approver chains, no approver-role registry, no multi-approver progress — so the rewired page has none either, and a gate leg refuses `PARALLEL_ANY`/`PARALLEL_ALL`/`SEQUENTIAL`/`APPROVER_REGISTRY`/`approverRoles` from re-entering the client. 🔑 **[[F2-199]]'s lesson, a second time in two slices: the fabrication was MORE granular than the platform's own model, which is exactly why it looked more finished.** |
| **⚠⚠ A ninth instrument, blind for a ninth reason: the fabricated-directory guard is keyed on ONE FILENAME** | [[F2-38]]c added a guard against fabricated user directories — `notificationsBackedByServer.test.ts`, whose `FAKE_DIRECTORY` constant is the literal module name `'lib/userDirectory'`. `APPROVER_REGISTRY` was a **second** fabricated directory, sixteen invented officers deep, in a file called `approvals.ts`, and therefore invisible to it. That is the same shape as [[F2-198]]'s finding about `demoFallbackContract`: **the invariant is real, its POPULATION is a filename.** |
| **⚠ Three dependents, all inside the fabricated estate, detached rather than repointed** | `assets.ts#approvalsForAsset` matched invented assets against invented approvals — two fabrications agreeing with each other — and is deleted; `AssetRegisterPage`'s "Approvals waiting" card and its KPI tile go with it. `AssetImpact.approvalCount` is **deleted, not zeroed**: nothing read it, and a hard 0 would have asserted *"no approvals waiting on this asset"*, which is [[F2-197]]'s invented all-clear. `mockWorkflows.ts#APPROVAL_WORKFLOWS` is now `[]` — it fed 12 synthesised rows into `ALL_WORKFLOWS`, the cross-module pulse, and is left empty rather than repointed because mixing one real async source into a corpus of invented ones gives a reader no way to tell which is which. `workflowChains.ts#fireFromApproval` + `CATEGORY_TO_EVENT` are deleted: their only caller was the page, firing a chain off a decision that was never persisted — a second, quieter fabrication on top of the first. |
| **⚠⚠ My own worst error, caught before it shipped: a dead-key detector that sweeps 71 keys** | Reconciling translations, I asked for `t('key')` and got **71 dead keys** — including ~57 `approvalChain*` ones and **`approvalsSidebar`**. Both were false: `t('approvalChainKpiInflight', 'In-flight')` is a **two-argument** call, so a pattern ending in `'\)` never matches it, and `approvalsSidebar` is referenced as `labelKey: 'approvalsSidebar'`, never through `t()`. Deleting them would have blanked five pages' labels and the sidebar row. Re-run with the rule [[F2-199]] used — *the quoted key appearing anywhere outside the translation files* — the honest answer is **11 dead, 12 new**. 🔑 **A usage detector must match every call shape the codebase uses, and the safe direction for a delete is to OVER-approximate usage.** Ninth instance in this lineage of a check satisfied by something other than its claim. |
| **⚠ And [[F2-165]]'s gate caught a dark method I had just written** | `approvalsApi.get` wrapped `GET /{id}`, which the server has and no screen opens. Rather than record it as dark, it is **not wrapped at all** — with a comment saying to add it in the commit that adds a detail view. An unused client method should not ship. |
| **New gate legs** | 11 in `pageDataProvenance.test.ts`. The load-bearing one is behavioural, not structural: *"no decision is written into local state — the row comes back from the server"*, because a rewire that kept a local status write would look identical on screen and be the same defect. Others pin the client to the real controller path, refuse a re-invented approver machine, refuse a `decidedBy` field the server ignores (the [[F2-184]] decoy shape), require `APPROVAL_TERMINAL` to be **derived** from the transition table rather than typed twice ([[F2-196]]'s rule), require an absent `slaDeadline` to read as unmeasured rather than on-track ([[F2-197]]'s rule), and forbid `useApiList` on this page because it prefers a demo corpus when the server returns zero rows — the load-bearing fallback that hid [[F2-158]]'s 500 for the whole Role API. |
| **Ratchets** | `BASELINE_STATE_CORPORA` **11 → 10**, `BASELINE_SIDEBAR_PAGES` **6 → 5**. Remaining sidebar members: `/assets`, `/attestations`, `/audit-workspace`, `/control-crosswalk`, `/regulatory-change`. |
| **Verified** | FE **590/590 across 59 files** (+11), `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean, census clean (no `fe_pages` drift — a `lib/` deletion does not move it). Mutation **12/12 as declared**, including the local-status-write mutation and one declared-SURVIVES negative control. **Live probe 17/17**: 22 real rows with 17 entity types; `?myInbox=true` as `admin` returns exactly its 3 PENDING rows; **`auditor` (WORKFLOW:WRITE, no APPROVE) is refused 403**; a `[REVIEW-TEST]` request created by `so_officer` came back `PENDING` **from the server**, was APPROVED with `decidedBy=so_officer` **taken from the principal**, refused a second decision with **409** because APPROVED is terminal, and **still read APPROVED on a fresh GET** — the persistence the old page never had. **A non-assignee holding APPROVE was refused 403**, so object-level ownership holds. Browser, through the Vite proxy: `lib/approvals.ts` fails to import, `approvalsApi.get` is `undefined`, `APPROVAL_TERMINAL` is `["APPROVED","REJECTED","EXPIRED"]` derived, and the register returns **23 rows / 12 PENDING**. |
| **⚠ Left behind, deliberately** | One `[REVIEW-TEST]`-tagged row (`APR-2026-19FF76EDDAD9F7A`, entity `POLICY / REVIEW-TEST-F2-201`) remains APPROVED in dev `approvals.requests`. Deleting it is a destructive DB operation and needs the owner's explicit OK (house rule 6); `DELETE` on this controller is PLATFORM_ADMIN-only in any case. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED.** `/approvals` decides through `POST /api/approvals/requests/{id}/transition`; `lib/approvals.ts` (407 lines, incl. the 16-role fabricated officer registry) deleted. 11 gate legs in `pageDataProvenance.test.ts`, the load-bearing one behavioural. Mutation 12/12; live probe 17/17. **0 backend changes, 0 migrations.** |
| **Filed** | **(a)** the **9 remaining corpora / 5 sidebar pages** in [[F2-198]]'s ratchets. **(b)** ⚠⚠ **`lib/platformPersistence.ts` — a global persistence-mode switch whose default is `'demo'` = pure `localStorage`**, persisted under `grc.persistence.mode.v1` and driving a topbar badge. It declares **11 adapters** but is imported by only **6** lib files, and `mirrorSaveToBackend` / `mirrorTransitionToBackend` / `mirrorDeleteToBackend` all `return` immediately in demo mode — so on the default setting the REST half is inert. Six adapters (`APPROVAL`, `CAPA`, `REGCHANGE`, `AUDIT_ENG`, `BOARD_PACK`, `NCA_ECC`) have no consumer beyond the `LIFECYCLE_ADAPTERS` map. `APPROVAL_ADAPTER` named `/api/approvals/requests` — the endpoint this finding wired — and nothing ever called it. **Needs its own slice**; it is the mechanism behind [[F2-196]]'s fourth DSR register. **(c)** `AssetImpact.riskCount` is a hard-coded `0` with the comment *"hooked up in production via Risk module — placeholder"* — the [[F2-197]] shape, on a page still in the ratchet. |

## F2-199 · The document a regulator receives was generated from a hard-coded corpus, and named the software vendor as the filing entity

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-199 *(measured 2026-08-12, immediately after [[F2-198]] — the first of the eleven pages [[F2-198]] filed, chosen because it was the one whose claim and whose truth were furthest apart. Lineage: [[F2-42]] → [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → this. Every earlier step asked what a **screen** asserts; this one asks what a screen **emits**.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2** — no control is bypassed and nothing is mis-stored, so not P1. But the artefact is a self-assessment addressed to the **National Cybersecurity Authority** under ECC-1/ECC-2, downloadable as CSV and printable to PDF, carrying CISO and CEO signature lines. Every earlier finding in this lineage misled somebody looking at a screen; this one hands them a file to sign. |
| **What was wrong, measured** | `/nca-ecc-export` was **routed, sidebar-linked (as the group header) and made no server call of any kind**. Its whole content came from `lib/ncaEcc.ts`'s `ECC_DOMAINS` — **30 controls across 4 domains**, each with an `implementation_status`, a maturity level `L1`–`L5`, an invented evidence reference (`POL-CYBER-001 v3.0`, `BOARD-PACK-Q2-2026`, `HR-LET-CISO-2024`) and a remark — plus six coverage `<Kpi>` tiles computed over them by `computeCoverage()`, a `buildCsv()` download and a `window.print()` path. The real register, probed live with two real personas and identical in **dev and prod**: `nca_ecc.filings` holds **4 filings** — FY2023 `ACKNOWLEDGED` (ref `NCA-ECC-2023-004812`), FY2024 `SUBMITTED` (ref `NCA-ECC-2024-006139`), FY2025 `CISO_APPROVAL`, FY2026 `PEER_REVIEW` — each with five per-domain scores, an overall score, a CAPA count, a peer reviewer and a CISO approver. FY2023 reads `[4,3,4,3,2]`, overall `3.2`. |
| **⚠⚠ The cover named the PRODUCT as the filer** | `ncaCoverEntity` rendered `t('brandName')` — **"TSS GRC Platform"**, the software this repo builds — beside a hard-coded commercial-registration number **`1010299292`**. On a multi-tenant platform that means *every* tenant's ECC return identified the vendor rather than the entity filing it, identically, with the same CR. 🔑 **A tenant-specific fact that appears as a literal in a shipped bundle cannot be right for more than one tenant, and is most likely right for none** — the same reasoning as [[F2-177]]'s `targetId` being a committee *type* rather than a PK, arrived at from the opposite direction. |
| **🔑 The fabrication was MORE GRANULAR than the platform's own filing model, which is why it looked more finished** | The ECC-2:2024 annual return is scored **per domain, 1–5** — that is what `nca_ecc.filings` models, what `NCA_DOMAINS` declares, and what `lib/ncaEccFiling.ts`'s own header comment says (*"self-assess across five domains and file an annual return"*). The retired page invented a **per-control matrix underneath** that: a finer-grained artefact than anything the platform tracks. It could not have been rebuilt honestly either — **`responses_json` is NULL on all 4 filings in both databases**, so per-control responses have never once been captured. Reconstructing them would have been [[F2-196]]'s defect. |
| **Fix — retired, not rewired** | ADR-017 §D-5, and the same call as [[F2-198]]: `NcaEccFilingsPage` already renders the real filings, the five domain scores, the gap summary, the submission reference and the whole `DRAFT → PEER_REVIEW → CISO_APPROVAL → SUBMITTED → ACKNOWLEDGED` workflow, so a second real ECC screen would have made two surfaces for one statutory object. `/nca-ecc-export` redirects to `/nca-ecc/filings` (F2-137 — a bookmark must land somewhere true); the sidebar group collapsed to its one real destination, because the old `ncaSidebar` label read literally **"NCA ECC export"**; `NcaEccExportPage.tsx`, `lib/ncaEcc.ts` and `ncaEcc.css` deleted (**1,013 lines**); **30 of the 31 `nca*` translation keys** removed from both languages, `ncaFilingsSidebar` the survivor. **0 backend changes, 0 migrations.** |
| **⚠ What was NOT rebuilt, and why** | The platform has **no server-side ECC export generator** — no endpoint, no POI/OpenPDF builder — so the export capability is a real gap, filed rather than hand-rolled: a client-side CSV of a regulator submission would bypass the export subsystem's RTL-Arabic handling and audit ledger, which is a product decision and not a fabrication fix. |
| **⚠⚠ Filed: THREE disjoint real ECC control registers, three different answers** | Identical in dev and prod. `cyber.cyber_controls` (framework `ECC-2:2024`) — **29 controls, every one `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, maturity NULL on all 29** (the register [[F2-195]] measured when it corrected the "NCA ECC Score 87%" tile to **0%**). `compliance.controls` where `framework = 'NCA_ECC'` — **14 rows: 6 `IMPLEMENTED` / 7 `PARTIAL` / 1 `PLANNED`**. `evidence.controls` for `ECC-2:2024` — **34 controls with no status column at all**. That is [[F2-196]]'s three-disjoint-DSR-registers shape, for the NCA ECC self-assessment. **Not resolved here**: picking a winner rewrites what the platform reports to a regulator, which is an owner decision — and it is precisely why no control-level coverage figure was put back on the submission surface. |
| **New gate — keyed on EMISSION, the question none of the seven existing instruments asks** | `src/__tests__/exportProvenance.test.ts`. Seven instruments now guard fabricated data and each is keyed on a mechanism: a filename (`demoFallbackContract`), a three-entry filename allow-list (F2-169's zero), an opt-in tag ([[F2-168]]), a hook (`isDemo`), a JSX tag ([[F2-195]]), a prop ([[F2-197]]), a routed component that calls nothing ([[F2-198]]). None asks whether the thing **producing a file** has server data behind it. Census: **21 files emit a document** (`Blob`/`.download`/`createObjectURL`/`window.print`); after the fix **zero routed pages** do so unbacked, so it ships as a **HARD ZERO with a deliberately EMPTY exemption map** — the sweep has landed, and house rule 3's warning applies. |
| **⚠⚠ My own first draft did exactly what [[F2-188]] warns about, and the REVERSE leg caught it** | I wrote two exemption entries with fluent multi-sentence reasons — `CsvImportPage` ("downloads an empty template") and `MfaSetupPage`, the latter a whole security narrative about browser-local MFA. **Both are Sprint 4 §3.3 CULLED pages**: routes removed, only the folders left on disk, so neither was ever in the population. The forward assertion passed — the population was already zero — and only *"every exemption names a page that is really in the population"* fired. 🔑 **A reason written for something that is not in the population reads exactly like a reason for something that is**, and the direction that catches it is the one nobody writes first. |
| **⚠⚠ A shared detector hole: the house idiom was invisible to both provenance gates** | `SERVER_CALL` was `\b\w*[Aa]pi\.\w+\s*\(` — and this codebase's idiom is a **typed** wrapper, `api.get<BoardPackAggregate>('/api/v1/reporting/board-pack.json')`, where a generic argument sits between the method name and the paren. **118 files** use that form. It surfaced as `BoardPackPage` being reported as having no server data in scope, when `lib/boardPackAggregate.ts` line 174 is a plain `api.get<T>(…)`. Fixed in **both** this gate and [[F2-198]]'s. ⚙ The error direction matters and is worth stating: it **over**-reports — a page that does call a server reads as one that never could — so it inflates a population rather than hiding one, the opposite of F2-198's comment-stripper bug. Re-measured after the fix, F2-198's eleven findings are unchanged, because none of them uses the generic form. |
| **⚠ And a one-hop rule must exclude the TRANSPORT** | Resolving "server data in scope" through one import hop marks any page importing `lib/api` as backed — but `lib/api.ts` contains `fetch(` **by definition**, so importing an `ApiError` type or a DTO from it is not evidence of use. A real call matches in the page itself and needs no hop. `TRANSPORT` excludes exactly `lib/api`, pinned in both directions by the synthetic self-test. |
| **⚠⚠ Second finding, in an existing gate: `routeReachability`'s own comment described a check that does not exist** | Its `INTENTIONALLY_OFF_NAV` header claimed *"if one of these ever becomes reachable … the test below says which."* The mutation harness disproved it — reverting a repointed `/ropa` link **SURVIVED**. And measuring showed the claim could not simply be promoted to an assertion: **2 of the 16 entries are legitimately linked** (`/login` from `Topbar`'s sign-out, `/portal/trust-center` from `PublicShell`'s public footer), because "off-nav" there means *not a sidebar destination*, not *nothing links it*. So the comment was corrected and the **enforceable** half added as `RETIRED_MUST_STAY_UNLINKED` — five retired redirects ([[F2-142]]'s three, [[F2-198]]'s `/ropa`, this one) that must have **zero** inbound links, plus the reverse leg that each is still a declared route so a bookmark cannot start 404ing. 🔑 **A comment describing a check that does not exist is worse than no comment, because it answers the question a reader was about to ask** — the [[F2-184]] shape, in a test's own documentation. |
| **⚠⚠ And it showed [[F2-198]]'s retirement was incomplete** | `/ropa` passed `routeReachability` not by exemption but because **four in-app links still pointed at it** — two data-flow-graph KPI tiles, one privacy-lifecycle tile, and `RopaWizard`'s post-publish `navigate('/ropa')`. F2-198 repointed the sidebar and left those bouncing through the redirect. All four now point at `/privacy?tab=ropa`. 🔑 **A retirement is not finished when the sidebar is repointed. A redirect keeps every stale link working — and that is exactly what stops anyone noticing they are stale**, including the orphan test, for which *being linked* is the passing condition. |
| **⚠ Two measurement errors of my own, both caught by running things** | **(a)** I guessed column names on `cyber.cyber_frameworks` (`name_en`) and got *"Invalid column name"* — which reads exactly like "the data isn't there". Resolve from `sys.columns`, not just `sys.tables`; that is the same lesson [[F2-198]] recorded one level up, and it recurred one level down. **(b)** The live probe asserted a deleted module 404s from Vite and reported **three false failures**: Vite's dev server has an **SPA fallback**, so a deleted path answers **200 with `index.html`**. The tell is `Content-Type` — `text/html` for the fallback, `text/javascript` for a real module. 🔑 **On an SPA dev server, HTTP 200 is not evidence that a file exists.** |
| **⚠ A structural check of my own was satisfied by prose** | Verifying the comment stripper, I counted declaration keywords before and after and "lost" 3 declarations in `lib/ncaEcc.ts`, 2 in `App.tsx` — because the words `export`, `type` and `return` appear in **header comments**. Anchored to line starts, the honest answer is **0 anchored declarations lost across all 773 files**, against **612 lost** by the wrong ordering. That negative control is stronger than [[F2-198]]'s single-file one, and it is the eighth instance in this lineage of a check satisfied by something other than its claim. |

Live probe **16/16**: `so_officer` (CYBER:READ) and `ranalyst` (COMPLIANCE:READ) both 200 with the 4 real filings and FY2023's real `[4,3,4,3,2]`/`3.2`/`NCA-ECC-2023-004812`, `responsesJson` NULL on all of them, the three retired modules answering `text/html` and the real one `text/javascript`. Backend doc-gated tests **21/21**. Census clean after updating **both** homes of `fe_pages` (352 → **351**; folders hold at **110** because `pages/nca-ecc/` still contains the real page — unlike `/ropa`, which took its folder with it). |

## F2-198 · A sidebar page invented the PDPL Article 31 register beside the real one, and every de-mocking gate was blind to it by construction

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-198 *(measured 2026-08-12, immediately after [[F2-197]] — the item [[F2-194]] filed and [[F2-197]] handed back. Lineage: [[F2-42]] → [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → this. Each step asks the question one level further out; this one asks it of the **page** rather than the component, which turns out to be the level at which every existing instrument has a hole.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2** — a statutory register (PDPL Art. 31, the record every Saudi DPO produces in an SDAIA inspection) rendered entirely from invented rows, sidebar-reachable, with a red "needs review" badge and a consent rollup claiming six-figure volumes. No control is bypassed and nothing is mis-stored, so not P1. |
| **What was wrong, measured** | `/ropa` was **routed, sidebar-linked, and made no server call of any kind** — 370 lines with zero `api.`/`useApiList`/`fetch`. Every figure came from `lib/ropaConsent.ts`: **9 invented processing activities**, five `<Kpi>` tiles computed over them by `aggregateRopa()` (total, consent-based, cross-border, reviewed-in-90-days, and **needs-review rendered `tone="danger"`**), a detail pane with categories/subjects/sub-processors/owner, and `CONSENT_SUMMARIES` asserting **142,310 active and 8,420 withdrawn consents** for one activity. The real register, probed live and identical in **dev and prod**: `privacy.processing_activities` **11 rows** — 5 cross-border, `LEGAL_OBLIGATION` 4 / `LEGITIMATE_INTEREST` 3 / `CONSENT` 2 / `CONTRACT` 2 — and `privacy.consents` **32 ACTIVE / 3 WITHDRAWN / 1 EXPIRED**. |
| **⚠⚠ Why every de-mocking instrument missed it — each is keyed on a MECHANISM this page does not use** | **(a)** `demoFallbackContract`'s ratchet counts `/mock/i` **imports** — a filename rule, so a corpus in `ropaConsent.ts` is invisible ([[F2-194]] already recorded this half). **(b)** The *same file's* F2-169 hard zero — *"fabricated data only substitutes for a fabricated parent"* — builds its population from `corpusNamesImportedBy`, which matches the module names `mock*`, `entityAnchors`, `policyLifecycle`. 🔑 **The invariant is real; its POPULATION is a filename allow-list**, and that had not been noticed. **(c)** [[F2-168]]'s `demoRows()`/`isDemoId()` tagging only reaches corpora that opted in, so [[F2-167]]'s `RowActions disabled={isDemo}` rule cannot fire on an untagged one. **(d)** The `isDemo` disclosure rule triggers on `useApiList`/`useApiResource`; a page that calls nothing is not a consumer. **(e)** [[F2-195]]'s `kpiProvenance` looks for a literal or a `\|\| N` fallback inside the `<Kpi>` tag — and `value={String(stats.total)}` where `stats = aggregateRopa()` is neither. |
| **🔑 The new shape: a CORRECT predicate over an INVENTED corpus** | `aggregateRopa` is honest arithmetic — it counts `lawfulBasis === 'CONSENT'`, it compares `lastReviewedAt` against a 90-day window. [[F2-195]]'s gate passes it because there is no literal; [[F2-196]]'s wrong-predicate gate would pass it too, because that gate assumes the rows are real. **Fourth shape in one lineage**: a literal (F2-195), a `\|\| N` fallback (F2-195), a wrong predicate over real rows (F2-196), a prop from a catalogue (F2-197) — and now a right predicate over rows that do not exist. |
| **⚠ Why it outlived the others: the clock** | `ropaConsent.ts` line 77 is `const _now = Date.now()` with `_daysAgo(n)` deriving every `lastReviewedAt` from it at module load. So "reviewed in the last 90 days" and "needs review" were computed against a clock that moves with the page load — [[F2-194]]'s rule exactly: **a clock-anchored fabrication has no tell**, where [[F2-193]]'s frozen 2026-05-05 stamps were visibly three months stale. Three of the surviving eleven pages do the same thing. |
| **Retired, not rewired — and that was the ratified answer** | `PrivacyPage`'s ROPA tab **already** renders the real register: `useApiList(() => privacyApi.ropa(0, 100))`, a five-column `DataTable`, `rowHref` to `/privacy/ropa/{id}`, and a real legal-basis breakdown. Building a second *real* ROPA screen would have created a fourth surface for one statutory object — precisely [[F2-196]]'s defect (three server-side DSR registers with disjoint vocabularies). ADR-017 §D-5 already chose *"retire the fabricated page"* for this shape in [[F2-42]]. So `/ropa` redirects to `/privacy?tab=ropa` ([[F2-137]] — a bookmark must land somewhere true) and the sidebar row points there directly. |
| **⚙ The sidebar handled it already** | `queryAwareActive` exists for exactly this (its docstring cites `/ndi?tab=cycles`), and `siblingsUseQuery` is derived per group as `group.items.some(s => s.to.includes('?'))` — so adding the query turns query-aware matching on for the privacy group automatically and the bare `/privacy` row stops double-highlighting. **Sixth** blocker in this programme that was already solved. |
| **⚠⚠ Two tiles were deliberately NOT rebuilt** | Probed live: the wire carries `crossBorderTransfer`, `legalBasis`, `retentionPeriodMonths`, `specialCategoryFlag` — and **no `lastReviewedAt`, no `nextReviewAt`**; neither column exists on the table in either database. So a review-currency figure could only have been invented, which is [[F2-196]]'s defect and [[F2-197]]'s trap. They are gone rather than em-dashed, because unlike a lifecycle tile there is no surviving component to hold the disclosure. |
| **The one signal preserved** | PDPL **Article 29** cross-border transfers — 5 of 11, real, and the fact a DPO is actually asked about. Now a tile on the surviving page, counted over the **same `ropa.data`** the activity count uses so the two can never disagree ([[F2-197]]'s rule). `crossBorderTransfer` was always on the wire because the endpoint returns the `ProcessingActivity` entity; `PrivacyRopaDto` simply never declared it, which is *why* the retired page invented its own count. 🔑 **Retiring a fabrication must not silently drop a real signal it happened to display.** |
| **⚠⚠ The measurement bug that nearly hid the whole population, in my own scan** | The census strips comments before parsing `App.tsx`. Written the obvious way — block comments first, then line comments — it deleted **40,247 of 89,522 characters, 45% of the file**, because line 122 is a `//` prose comment whose text contains a literal `/*`: the block pattern ran from there to the next closing delimiter and took the `lazy()` declarations for the very pages being measured. The census reported **24** server-less pages instead of **74**, and **0** sidebar-reachable state-asserting instances instead of **8** — so `/ropa`, `/assets`, `/control-crosswalk` and `/crisis-management`, all four already known, were silently absent. 🔑 **A corrupted source yields a SMALLER population, which reads exactly like "those pages are fine"** — the quietest way for a scan to be wrong, and the **seventh** instance in this programme of a detector satisfied by something other than its claim. Fix: **one alternation, left-to-right** (`(?<!:)//[^\n]*\|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/`), so at a `//` an inner `/*` can never open a block and at a `/*` a URL cannot truncate the block. Pinned in both directions, plus a leg asserting the real `App.tsx` keeps >75% of its bytes and still yields ≥250 routed components. ⚠⚠ **And this was a REPEAT, not a discovery — the repo already held the rule and the reason.** `Appendix/scripts/baseline_census.py` lines 139–142 carry the correct ordered alternation with a comment naming this exact failure: *"Getting this wrong in the OTHER direction is what F2-68(c) found in the frontend scanner: strip block comments first and a `//` line containing a block-OPEN marker swallows the file to the next CLOSE marker."* I wrote a second scanner over the same tree without reading the first one and reproduced the bug it warns about. 🔑 **Before writing a scanner, read the scanner this repo already has** — same shape as F2-195's `|| N`, where the codebase held the correct rule in prose three lines from where it was not applied, and as F2-179's "read the code before believing a doc's claim about it, including one you wrote." |
| **The population, measured properly** | Over **310 routed components**: **73 pages make no server call at all**, **47 of them sidebar-reachable**. Most are legitimate — a wizard that posts elsewhere, a label map, an options list — so it is narrowed by [[F2-193]]'s ratified rule (a catalogue may declare what a thing IS, never what is happening to it now): **14 corpora on 12 pages, 8 sidebar-reachable, 5 clock-minted**. Retiring `/ropa` took that to **12 / 11 / 7 / 3**. The sidebar-reachable remainder: `/approvals` (`APPROVAL_REQUESTS` 17, clock-minted) · `/assets` (`ASSETS` 19) · `/attestations` (`ATTESTATION_CAMPAIGNS` 24) · `/audit-workspace` (`AUDIT_APPOINTMENTS` 13 + `AUDIT_COMMITTEE_MEETINGS` 21) · `/control-crosswalk` (`MASTER_CONTROLS` 72) · `/nca-ecc-export` (`ECC_DOMAINS` 40) · `/regulatory-change` (`REGULATORY_CHANGES` 14, clock-minted). |
| **⚠ A ratchet, deliberately, and with no narrated reasons** | House rule 3's warning — a ceiling makes a tolerated site indistinguishable from a reviewed one — applies *once a sweep has landed*. Eleven pages remain, each a separate capability question, so the honest instrument is one that stops the population growing and prints what is left. And **no per-page reasons are written**: [[F2-188]]'s failure mode was manufacturing fluent prose for a population nobody had verified, and I have verified only that these pages call nothing and that their corpora assert a status. ⚠ I did **not** establish whether each has a real backend — a first attempt guessed six table names and **five did not exist**, the same guessed-path error as [[F2-197]]'s probe. The next slice must resolve them from `sys.tables`, per page. |
| **Verification** | FE **564/564 across 58 files** (+15 tests, +1 file). `tsc` clean. `vite build` clean — the `RopaPage` chunk is gone from the bundle. Mutation **11/11 as declared** (10 caught, 1 declared SURVIVES: a ratchet cannot detect its own ceiling being raised, which is what review and this entry are for). Live probe **11/11** on `GET /api/v1/privacy/ropa` through the Vite proxy. In the running app `/ropa` resolves to **`/login?next=%2Fprivacy%3Ftab%3Dropa`** — the redirect fires before the auth gate and `next` preserves the real tab — and all three retired modules fail to import while `privacyApi.ropa` is still a function. Pre-fix control: the same detector reads **14 corpora / 8 sidebar pages** on master, both above the new baseline, so the ratchet would have failed there. **0 backend changes, 0 migrations.** |
| **⚠ One thing the green first run did not prove** | All 15 assertions passed immediately, which is also what a rotted regex looks like ([[F2-195]]). One did fail on a second look and is worth recording: `/^\s+ropaSidebar: '/m` demanded a single space after the colon, and the translation files **column-align** their values (`ropaSidebar:             'ROPA',`). A key-existence assertion that is too strict about whitespace fails loudly, which is the safe direction — but the same regex written as a *negative* check would have passed while proving nothing. |
| **Status** | ✔ **CLOSED.** `pageDataProvenance.test.ts` (15 tests): two decrease-only ratchets (12 corpora, 7 sidebar pages) that print the offenders on failure; a three-part anti-vacuity leg (≥250 routed components, ≥40 server-less pages, ≥8 findings) because both ratchets pass trivially if the scan resolves nothing — which is exactly what the broken stripper did; four comment-stripper integrity legs; and eight `/ropa` legs — the files are gone, nothing imports them, the route redirects (asserted on the whole `<Route>` element, not the bare word `Navigate`, which appears in this file's own prose), the sidebar points at the tab and no row still routes to `/ropa`, the surviving surface calls `privacyApi.ropa(` **as a call** and not as an import ([[F2-194]]'s twice-lost mutation), the cross-border figure derives from `ropa.data`, the new label is bilingual, and the 45 retired keys are absent from both languages while `ropaSidebar` survives. |
